content: Co-codamol is a non-proprietary name that refers to a combination of codeine phosphate and paracetamol (also known as acetaminophen). Co-codamol tablets are used to alleviate mild to moderate pain, and in the case of the 30/500 mg formulation, they are also effective for severe pain. There are three available strengths of co-codamol: 8 mg of codeine phosphate per tablet 15 mg of codeine phosphate per tablet 30 mg of codeine phosphate per tablet The 30 mg strength is available in capsules under the brand names Tylex and Kapake, and in tablet form as Solpadol. The formulations also contain between 300 mg and 1000 mg of paracetamol per tablet. In the United Kingdom, the 500 mg paracetamol + 15 mg codeine and 500 mg paracetamol + 30 mg codeine tablets are only available with a prescription. However, the 500 mg paracetamol + 8 mg codeine strength can be purchased over the counter. Similarly, in Australia, the 500 mg + 15 mg tablets in packs of 12 or fewer are classified as Schedule 3 (Pharmacist Only Medicine), while higher strengths require a prescription. Manufacturers recommend not exceeding the dosage of two tablets every four hours, with a maximum of eight tablets in a 24-hour period. It is advised to avoid taking other medications containing paracetamol concurrently to prevent overdose. In the United States, Tylenol 4 contains 60 mg of codeine and 300 mg of paracetamol per tablet. Tylenol with Codeine products in the U.S. do not contain caffeine. However, in Canadian preparations, Tylenol 2 and 3 include 15 mg of caffeine. Co-codamol is marketed under different names in various countries: in the U.S. and Canada as Tylenol 3 with Codeine, in the UK as Solpadeine and Solpadol, and in Australia as Panadeine, Panadeine 15, and Panadeine Forte. Side Effects The potential side effects of co-codamol include: Skin rashes and hypersensitivity reactions Constipation Fainting (syncope or near-syncope) Nausea and/or vomiting Confusion Loss of short-term memory Drowsiness Changes in blood composition Easy bruising and bleeding gums
